title: CoreGate: Execution-Lineage Supervision for Attack Technique Recognition under Environment Shift
description:
Reference implementation and released experiment artifacts for CoreGate, which converts process associations recorded in execution journals into training-only foreground supervision for attack-technique recognition. The targets require neither technique labels nor technique-specific rules, and inference reads only the observed graph.

The deposit contains the encoder and gated-readout training code, the locked four-fold three-seed leave-one-environment-out results (CoreGate-Lineage 95.92% accuracy / 95.44% macro-F1 vs. Ordinary 91.73% / 92.92%, +129 parameters), the learned-attention, shuffled-target and SAGPool controls, the joint environment/template holdout with edge-rank permutation controls, the template-disjoint and embedding-only classifier diagnostics, the process-only and context-union sensitivities, the three-view statistics audit, the target-deletion curve, and the dataset metadata and catalog.

The 360-graph attack-emulation dataset is a separate deposit and is released upon acceptance of the accompanying paper. Targets are automatically derived weak supervision rather than independently validated attack evidence, so the release documents a within-catalog recognition gain rather than causal or cross-host validation.
